title: Keep the planted-violation harness (16 plants, xUnit versus Fitness, plus the divergence shapes) in the repo, with a check that ArchitectureRulesTests and fitness.yaml patterns still agree
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

Does the person want the parity check wired into the test suite (RuleCopiesAgreeTests launches powershell.exe on every `dotnet test`), or left as a script under eng/ that someone must remember to run? The design wires it, so drift fails a gate instead of depending on memory. Deleting that one file reverses it, at the cost of the header comment being the only automatic guard again.

Is it acceptable that the behavioural harness (C1/C2) runs only where the TAAD engine checkout exists and is never part of a routine test run? It is kept in the repo and cannot run from a clean clone. Only the parity check (C3) runs anywhere.

Parity in PowerShell and the harness in Python (two languages under eng/), versus one language for both. Python for the parity check would make every test run depend on an interpreter the platform constraint cannot assume; PowerShell for the harness would need a Python bridge to taad3 anyway.

A shelling Fact in Core.Tests as the permanent caller, versus a script-only check that someone must remember to run. The slice text says 'lives under eng/ as a script'; the Fact is the one addition beyond it.
Pairing entries to Facts by pattern content, versus an explicit twin-name map. Content pairing needs no third file but cannot see a scope entry dropped from one of a split Fact's two.
Plants and divergences as JSON data files beside harness.py, versus inline literals in the script.
The name and location eng/rules-harness/ with harness.py, plants.json and divergences.json, versus a flat eng/ layout or a single README-documented script.
Tagging the divergence prose at fitness.yaml:21-34 with D-ids, versus leaving the header prose as the SL-022 author wrote it.
The TAAD3_BACKEND environment fallback for the engine root, dropped per O-004 (see deviations).
The optional switch of run_fitness() to a taad_v3 CLI. The design said the build 'may'. In-process import through one adapter function was kept.

No plant or exemption row covers FileSystemCallsGoThroughTheCancelGuard (SL-024) or its except_files (Kernel32.cs, SynchronousIoCancel.cs). TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls is covered only through F03's 'also'. A scope or exemption drift on those rules is invisible to both tools until a person adds rows with measured outcomes.
The 7 settled entries (SL-023, SL-024, SL-031) have no behavioural coverage and no xUnit twin. The harness only confirms they are clean and matched on the real tree.

The engine's file-writing tools turn a '\uXXXX' sequence in written content into the character itself: '﻿' was stored as U+FEFF in three files before I caught it. Anyone editing the BOM-guard lines of .taad/fitness.yaml, or writing such escapes through those tools, needs [char]92 or chr() constructions. Worth fixing in the engine.

The design-slice open questions are still for a person. Should the parity Fact run on every `dotnet test` (it does now; deleting RuleCopiesAgreeTests.cs reverses it)? Is a harness that runs only where the taad_v3 checkout exists acceptable?

pwsh 7's -eq/-ceq on strings compares by culture and ignores ICU-ignorable characters such as U+0001 and U+FEFF. Any other repo PowerShell that compares pattern or path text with -ceq could hide a difference, so an audit may be worthwhile.
